findings.summary: No rollback path for users already converted to JWT — they lose auth entirely
findings.explanation: Step 6 rollback disables the JWT path via feature flag but says nothing about users holding a JWT and no session cookie. Those users lose authentication on rollback.

findings.summary: No day-1 failure handling when the token refresh endpoint is unavailable
findings.explanation: Step 2 defines 15-minute access tokens and 7-day refresh tokens but never describes refresh-endpoint failure. Users with expired access tokens and a down refresh service are locked out.

findings.summary: New auth service never sized for the 50,000 DAU target; refresh-token store is a new bottleneck
findings.explanation: The motivation is scaling to 50,000 DAU, but the plan never sizes the JWT service for that load. Refresh-token storage in its own database is a new stateful bottleneck that can hit the same wall as Redis sessions.

findings.summary: Causal chain break — clients have no signal telling them to exchange sessions for JWTs
findings.explanation: Step 4 produces a unified internal auth context from either method, so the gateway silently accepts both. Step 5 expects clients to exchange sessions for JWTs, but nothing signals them to migrate. The lazy migration trigger is undefined.

x-falsePositiveTraps.description: Section 3's Datadog dashboards, structured logging with correlation IDs, and the decision to stand monitoring up before rollout are genuinely well designed.
x-falsePositiveTraps.expected_outcome: The observability structure and its ordering before rollout are sound. NOTE (corrected 2026-09-01): the alert thresholds are NOT part of this trap. PagerDuty pages at >100ms against a p99 <50ms SLO and at >0.5% error against a 99.9% (0.1%) success SLO, so the alerts fire only well after the SLO is breached. Both arms flagged it correctly.

x-falsePositiveTraps.description: The RS256 decision in Step 1 is well-justified — asymmetric signing for multi-service token verification is a legitimate security architecture choice.
x-falsePositiveTraps.expected_outcome: Socratic why-chain should terminate in a supported axiom (asymmetric crypto for a multi-verifier topology), not flag this as a flaw. Both arms credited it explicitly in the 2026-09-01 run — this trap works as designed.

x-knownUnseededDefects: Step 3 alert thresholds sit above the stated SLOs (100ms vs 50ms p99; 0.5% vs 0.1% error), so monitoring cannot catch an SLO breach in time. Real defect, not seeded.
'Zero user-facing auth errors during migration' contradicts the 99.9% success-rate metric in the same list. Real defect, not seeded.
